 Central Government DA Hike: Current Rate, Salary Calculations, And Pending July Revision
 Central government employees currently receive DA at 60 per cent of their basic pay, while the July 2026 revision is yet to be announced by the Centre
 O Outlook Money Curated by: Priyanka Debnath Updated on: 21 October 2026 10:22 am Updated on: 21 October 2026 10:22 am SUBSCRIBE 
 Central Government DA Hike 2026 Photo: AI generated Central Government DA Hike 2026 Photo: AI generated Summary of this article
 July 2026 DA revision is pending official government approval.
 Current DA rate stands at 60 per cent of basic pay.
 Pensioners receive dearness relief linked to the DA revision.
 Central government employees are awaiting an official announcement on the dearness allowance (DA) revision for July 2026. The Union Cabinet is scheduled to discuss the matter on October 21, 2026,  but the government has not confirmed whether the pending revision will be on the agenda.
 DA is paid to central government employees to help offset the impact of inflation. The current rate is 60 per cent of basic pay , following the previous revision approved in April 2026. The next rate and announcement date have not been officially confirmed.

 BY Outlook Money 
 DA Revision For July 2026 
 The Centre revises DA twice a year, once in January, and later in July. However, the date of the announcement can vary. The Cabinet meeting held on October 14 did not bring an announcement on the pending July revision. As on October 20, the Centre has not officially confirmed the new DA rate or when the revision will be approved.
 The next Cabinet meeting is scheduled for October 21. Whether the government will announce the pending revision at this meeting can only be confirmed through an official communication.
 Continue Reading Current DA Rate And Salary Calculation 
 In April 2026, the Union Cabinet approved a 2 percentage point increase in DA, taking it from 58 per cent to 60 per cent. The revised rate took effect from January 1, 2026.
 The amount employees receive as DA depends on their basic pay . For an employee with a basic salary of Rs 44,900, DA at the current rate of 60 per cent amounts to Rs 26,940 per month. If the DA rate was 63 per cent, the allowance for the same basic salary would amount to Rs 28,287 per month. This would be Rs 1,347 more each month, or Rs 16,164 over 12 months.
 These figures are calculations based on a hypothetical rate of 63 per cent. They do not represent an officially approved increase. The actual amount payable will depend on the rate notified by the government.
 Dearness Relief For Central Government Pensioners 
 Central government pensioners receive dearness relief (DR) , which is revised in line with DA. The purpose of these allowances is to help pensioners cushion the impact of inflation on their pension income. 
 DR amount depends on the applicable rate and the pensioner’s basic pension. Pensioners are advised to crosscheck any claim about changes in the rates with official government sources before passing on the information. As on October 20, the Centre has not officially announced the July 2026 revision.
